To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
parkin, a protein involved in mitochondrial quality control, regulates the ER-mitrochondrial inter-organelles crosstalk and Ca(2+) fluxes, thus modulating the cellular ATP production.
parkin over-expression favors the ER-mitochonria crosstalk, increasing the mitochondrial calcium uptake and the agonist induced ATP production.
parkin is a novel modulator of the ER-mitochrondria cross talk and that parkin over-expression increases ER-mitochondrial tethering, mitochondrial Ca(2+)-uptake and ATP production.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of new functions of parkin in the modulation of ER-mitochondrial cross talk, which could contribute to a better understanding of the mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of Parkinson disease.
the role played by parkin in the modulation of the ER-mitrochondria crosstalk, a mechanism that may represent a novel protective mechanism against mitochondrial stress.
the characterization of the role of parkin in the maintenance of mitochondrial Ca(2+)-signaling and bioenergetics under physiological conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

parkin, in the absence of mitochondrial stress and dysfunction, plays a role in the maintenance and the modulation of the ER-mitochonrial crosstalk, thus contributing to the regulation of Ca(2+) and bioenergetics.

parkin is a key player in the maintenance of the ER-mitochonria crosstalk, which in turn is essential for the maintenance of cellular Ca(2+) balance and ATP production, and therefore for cell survival.

the parkin overexpression favors the ER-mitochrondria tethering, increases the mitochondrial Ca(²⁺) uptake and the mitochondrial ATP synthesis, thus suggesting that the parkin upregulation may represent an adaptive mechanism to sustain cell bioenergy production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
parkin could act as a molecular link to coordinate the ER-mitochrondria crosstalk to sustain cell homeostasis.
parkin over-expression could favor ER-mitochonria cross-talk, thus promoting a better cellular bioenergetic efficiency and Ca(2+) buffering.
parkin over expression enhances ER-mitochondrion crosstalk by promoting the transfer of Ca(2+) from the ER to mitochondria and this favors ATP production in the cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the overexpression of parkin in model cells physically enhances ER-mitochondrial coupling, favors Ca(2+) flux from the ER to mitochondria following cells treatment with agonists and increases agonist-induced ATP synthesis.
parkin over-expression could be a useful strategy to counteract ER stress, mitochondrial stress and mitochondrial dysfunction.
parkin is a novel player in the ER-mitochrondria crosstalk, and that its overexpression is protective for cells exposed to ER stress.
